title: Expanding small-business support eligibility toward larger firms can crowd out smaller firms' revenue, wages, exits, and innovation
source_unit: US administrative Census firm data around quasi-random timing of expanded small-business program eligibility; NBER Working Paper 35703, issued September 2026

observations.period: 2026 NBER working-paper evidence; timing of expanded eligibility and subsequent firm outcomes

denominator.unit: Administrative Census firm universe; exact analytical counts are not exposed on the official abstract page

smallest_firm_revenue.value: Revenue declines after eligibility expands toward larger firms, especially for younger, more productive, and financially constrained small firms

government_contracts.value: Government procurement contracts are reallocated to larger firms

firm_exit.value: Firm exits increase among the affected smaller firms

wages.unit: causal firm/labor outcome; exact universe not exposed in abstract

observations.method: Use the official NBER abstract's quasi-random timing design and administrative Census outcomes; preserve the paper's claim about eligibility expansion and the distinct revenue, procurement, exit, wage, and patenting outcomes without reconstructing effect sizes.
observations.uncertainty: The retained evidence is abstract-level and does not expose program identity, thresholds, analytical counts, effect sizes, standard errors, treatment timing, contract quality, worker hours/benefits, customer prices, owner-household outcomes, or local service changes. Crowding out is a study interpretation tied to the paper's design, not a universal result for every support program.
observations.subgroup: Small firms, especially younger, more productive, and financially constrained firms, compared with larger firms gaining eligibility; exact subgroup universes remain paper-specific.
observations.counterinterpretation: Larger firms may deliver scale, quality, resilience, or more jobs; contract reallocation is not automatically social harm. Lower small-firm revenue or exits can coexist with lower prices or better service, which the source does not measure.

related_sources.claim: The committed project packet records the official NBER source, causal design summary, counterpoint, and open fields.
The official NBER page provides the current abstract and citation for Working Paper 35703.

boundary: This record closes an eligibility-rule-to-firm-allocation and small-firm-outcome arrow for the studied US program setting. It does not establish customer welfare, worker security beyond the reported wage direction, owner-household recovery, public legitimacy, political action, or a general rule about support scale.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Existing local source-search packet and official NBER paper page; no working-paper PDF, code, administrative data, or microdata retained
